svg.text: The piece is a chain: each section's gap forces the next idea, running from the problem (how can billions of
neurons coordinate fast) down through oscillations, a specific wave theory, and anesthesia evidence, converging on
one synthesis that is then checked against rival theories.

g.text: A single argument builds floor by floor: synapses alone can't explain flexible cognition, so the paper looks to brain
waves, builds a specific theory of how they control spiking, tests it against traveling waves and anesthesia, then
lands on one hybrid framework and checks it against rivals.

g.title: Flexible thought needs fast, brain-wide coordination — → spya-f6m6jv
Classical view: fixed, specialized neurons can't explain this — → spya-k046f6
Neurons multiplex many roles at once — → spya-v0gbwq
Waves organize & route neural signals — → spya-jnp59d
Waves alter spiking directly (ephaptic) — → spya-mapqhv
These converge: waves can flexibly steer spiking
g.text: These converge: waves can flexibly steer

g.title: Alpha/beta waves as inhibitory "stencils" over gamma/spiking — → spya-qck2sw
Explains mixed selectivity — → spya-zmknun
Explains subspace coding — → spya-m63zb9
Confirmed in primate PFC — → spya-azz3c8
Traveling waves shift coding states; wave interference computes — → spya-y09vju
Anesthesia: diverse drugs all desynchronize waves — → spya-uvev07
Hybrid synapse/wave framework for cognition & consciousness — → spya-dnv2tp

g.text: SPATIAL COMPUTING: A SPECIFIC WAVE THEORY
Three independent lines of evidence — multifunctional neurons, wave organization, and direct electrical (ephaptic)
effects — converge on the idea that waves, not synapses alone, could flexibly route information.

g.title: A task engages ~1/3 of prefrontal neurons — → spya-amx5qf
So neurons must be multifunctional, not specialized — → spya-v0gbwq
Mixed selectivity: a neuron's response changes with context — e.g. object A only if seen first — → spya-x5m34h
g.text: e.g. object A only if seen first

g.title: This needs flexible routing, hard for fixed synapses alone — → spya-dtnkkk
Oscillations organize, route, and time information exchange — → spya-jnp59d
Ephaptic coupling: fields directly shift spike timing, fast & widely — → spya-mapqhv
Waves can flexibly coordinate huge populations of neurons — → spya-f59f0p

g.text: One mechanism (alpha/beta as inhibitory stencils over gamma spiking) is shown to explain two separate puzzles, mixed
selectivity and subspace coding, and then is extended in time (traveling waves) and in kind (analog computation).

g.title: Alpha/beta stencils suppress gamma/spiking by location — → spya-hcav4k
Same neuron: suppressed in one context, active in another — → mixed selectivity — → spya-zmknun
Stencils split population activity into separate subspaces — → subspace coding — → spya-m63zb9
Confirmed in primate prefrontal cortex — → spya-azz3c8
Traveling waves move the stencil, shifting activity between subspaces — → spya-mrsvfu
Waves can also directly compute, not just gate — → spya-h5qjz4

g.title: Analog computation: continuous, parallel, interference-based — → spya-vp5h33
Far more energy-efficient than digital computing — → spya-mgnqxk
Overlapping context-waves could compute task combinations — → spya-prykb8
